coverage: Read every line of: server/elevation.ts 1-79, server/escpos.ts 1-1, server/growthRoutes.ts 1-552, server/httpConditional.ts 1-6, server/index.ts 1-205, server/keepAlivePing.ts 1-16, server/logBuffer.ts 1-11, server/principalCache.ts 1-56, server/printRoutes.ts 1-635, server/printService.ts 1-115, server/realtime/publisher.ts 1-170. Spot-checked storage.updateOrder, auditService.logAudit signature, client callers of /api/print/ack, /api/coupons/apply, /api/loyalty/redeem, /api/automation/birthday/run, /api/digest/run. Did not read couponService/loyaltyService/razorpayService bodies in full.

findings.title: POST /api/automation/birthday/run is requireAuth but force-sends real WhatsApp messages
findings.detail: The route calls runBirthdayAutomation({ force: true }) behind only requireAuth. CLAUDE.md treats the analogous POST /api/automation/run (force-triggers a real outbound send batch) as a ban-risk surface and gates it requireAdmin; this sibling route was left at requireAuth.
findings.failure_scenario: Any staff-tier PIN session (or a script with its cookie) POSTs /api/automation/birthday/run repeatedly; each call forces a birthday send run to customers, bypassing the scheduler's once-per-day gating intent and raising WhatsApp ban risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate with requireAdmin, matching /api/automation/run and /api/automation/config. Consider the same for /api/digest/run (sends the owner digest) and /api/feedback/schedule (queues a customer message).

findings.title: Coupon apply / loyalty redeem rewrite totals of paid or cancelled orders and race on discount
findings.detail: Both routes load the order, consume the coupon/points, then storage.updateOrder(discountAmount, taxAmount, totalAmount) with no check of paymentStatus/status and no conditional WHERE. newDiscount = order.discountAmount (read before redeem) + result.discount, so two concurrent applies to the same order each read the same base discount and the second write overwrites the first.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Billing applies a coupon to an order already settled: totalAmount drops while paidAmount stays, so Reports' net revenue (totalAmount - shortfall) changes after the fact and the order looks overpaid. (b) Two coupons applied near-simultaneously to one order: both redemptions are recorded (coupons consumed) but only one discount lands on the bill. (c) Loyalty redeem with an orderId of a cancelled order deducts points onto a dead order.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject unless paymentStatus='pending' and status<>'cancelled'; do the redemption and the order update in one transaction with the order row locked (or a conditional UPDATE computing discount_amount = discount_amount + $d in SQL).

findings.title: order.coupon_applied / order.loyalty_redeemed audit rows are fire-and-forget
findings.detail: logAudit(...) is not awaited before res.json at lines 355 and 453. CLAUDE.md requires order/money deviation audit rows to be awaited because Vercel can freeze the function after the response, losing the row.
findings.failure_scenario: On Vercel a coupon discount is applied and the response returns; the function is frozen before the audit INSERT runs, so Reports -> KOT & Bill Activity has no record of the discount.
findings.suggested_fix: await logAudit(...) before responding in both routes.

findings.title: Loyalty points deducted even when the supplied orderId does not exist
findings.detail: order is null when orderId is given but not found; redeemPoints still runs and the discount branch is skipped (order && ...), so points are consumed with no discount applied anywhere, and the route returns ok:true with the discount amount.
findings.failure_scenario: Client sends a stale/merged-away orderId (merge deletes the source order); the customer's points are debited, response says ok with discount ₹X, but no bill is discounted.
findings.suggested_fix: If orderId is provided and the order is not found (or not editable), return 404/409 before calling redeemPoints.

findings.title: Razorpay: client-chosen amount and client-chosen posOrderId let a small payment mark any order paid
findings.detail: create-order accepts amount from the body (Number(amount) || total) and verify marks Number(posOrderId) (from the body) paid after verifying only the Razorpay signature — never checking that the Razorpay order belongs to that POS order or that the captured amount covers its total. It uses plain updateOrder (no settleOrderIfUnpaid guard, so a cancelled order is resurrected to served+paid and loyalty/feedback can fire twice). Note: CLAUDE.md says Razorpay is out of scope by standing instruction; reported for the owner's awareness, not as a requested fix.
findings.failure_scenario: Staff creates a Razorpay order with amount 1 for a ₹1,200 bill, pays ₹1, and the verify call marks the order paid; or pays a ₹1 order for POS order A and sends posOrderId=B to mark B paid.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore client amount/posOrderId: derive the POS order from getPosOrderForRazorpay(razorpay_order_id), compare the stored Razorpay amount to the order total, and settle through settleOrderIfUnpaid.

findings.title: Razorpay webhook verifies signature against JSON.stringify(req.body), not the raw bytes
findings.detail: index.ts only stashes rawBody for /api/whatsapp/webhook. Re-serializing the parsed body does not reliably reproduce Razorpay's exact payload bytes (escaped slashes/unicode, number formatting), the same reason CLAUDE.md gives for the Meta webhook's rawBody capture.
findings.failure_scenario: A genuine payment.captured webhook whose body contains an escaped character or a float like 1.0 fails HMAC and gets 401; the order is never marked paid via webhook.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture rawBody for /api/razorpay/webhook in the express.json verify hook (both entries) and HMAC that buffer.

findings.title: Server-side USB (libusb) send leaks the device on claim failure and does not await release
findings.detail: If iface.claim() or detachKernelDriver() throws, device.close() is never called. On success/failure the release is iface.release(true, cb) fire-and-forget inside the transfer callback, so the promise resolves before the interface is freed — the same race CLAUDE.md documents and fixed in desktop/print/usbLibusb.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: On a persistent Linux/mac server with a USB printer, a KOT and Bill sent back-to-back: the second open/claim races the still-releasing first and fails; or a claim error leaves the device open so every later print fails until restart.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap open/claim in try/finally closing the device, and await release via a Promise before resolving, mirroring usbLibusb.ts.

findings.title: Test print uses server-local time and E.centered under ALIGN_CENTER
findings.detail: new Date().toLocaleString('en-IN') formats in the server's ambient timezone (CLAUDE.md: always formatISTDateTime for printed output), and E.centered(...) is used while E.ALIGN_CENTER is active, which CLAUDE.md documents as double-centering.
findings.failure_scenario: On a non-IST host the test page shows a UTC time; the printer name/time lines drift right of the natively-centred title.
findings.suggested_fix: Use formatISTDateTime and plain E.line() under ALIGN_CENTER.

findings.title: Razorpay verify crashes with 500 after recording success when posOrderId matches no order
findings.detail: storage.updateOrder returns undefined for a non-existent id; (updated as any).tableId then throws TypeError, after markTransactionSuccess already ran.
findings.failure_scenario: Client sends a stale posOrderId; transaction marked success, response is a 500, checkout UI reports failure for a captured payment.
findings.suggested_fix: Check updated before dereferencing and return 404.

findings.title: GET /api/feedback with non-numeric limit passes NaN to LIMIT
findings.detail: parseInt('abc') is NaN; Math.min(NaN,200) is NaN; .limit(NaN) produces an invalid SQL LIMIT and a 500. Same at /api/digest/history.
findings.failure_scenario: ?limit=all returns 500 instead of a default page.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to the default when the parsed value is not a positive finite number.
